rule:
For each figure file the run wrote (stability-B2.md, fidelity-B3.md, position-B3.md,
transmission-B4.md, transmission-after-revision-B4.md), every line that names fidelity, alpha, Jaccard, stability,
transmission, position or agreement and holds a number, with its line number: the figures as the run stated them.
The verdict fleet's disagreement rate is recomputed from verdicts-D.jsonl: of the first return's rooms with two or more
readers, those whose readers' verdicts are not all the same. FLEET.md section 2's definitions are printed beside them
(the lines of that section that name the same words). What each licenses is written in the audit section; none of
them is called reliability or intra-rater.

stability-B2.md.text: **Stability: 0.807** (primary placements alike in 0.853 of the cross pairs).
| stab-1 against stab-2, mean Jaccard over the nine reader pairs per item | 0.807 |
| pairwise agreement inside the gold round | 0.818 |
| alpha over the six stability readers | 0.784 |
| mean change of an item's fidelity between stab-1 and stab-2 | 0.076 |

**What it shows.** Readers given differently worded briefs agree with each other (0.807) as much as readers given the same brief do (0.800 and 0.756). The rewording adds no disagreement beyond what three fresh readers already show under one brief. So about one placement in five differs between reade
**Fidelity under the rewordings.** It barely moves: 0.624 for gold, 0.636 for stab-1, 0.631 for stab-2. The primary match with my placement is 0.800 in all three.

fidelity-B3.md.text: Each seeded gold copy is scored against my placement in `gold_items.jsonl` (Jaccard), against the rechecked placement, on exact set and on primary match. The B2 figure for the same copy is the mean over B2's nine frozen-scheme readings of that item (the gold round, stab-1, stab-2). The fall is B2 mi

**The fall** in fidelity over the whole fleet is -0.014 (95% interval over batches -0.031 to 0.003). It is inside the floor of 0.193. The fleet's gold fidelity did not fall against B2 on the same items; group 2 went out on that ground and held it.
**The corpus readings of gold items** (the live readings, apart from the seeded copies): 80 lines, fidelity 0.683, primary 0.850.

position-B3.md.text: Pooled across the fleet, pass 1, corpus copies with both replicates returned. Three outcomes per line: agreement (Jaccard with the other replicate's line on the same item), multi (more than one theme) and arguable (confidence "arguable"). Each is regressed on position within the batch with batch fix
| outcome | slope per position | SE | change over 14 | 95% interval | sensitivity over 14 | within the tolerance |

fleet_md_section_2_lines: | **fidelity** | how often a reader holding only the frozen instrument lands where you did in `author_items` | your own answered items |

| **agreement** | how often the `R` readers of one item agree with each other; reported with Krippendorff's alpha on the overlap, with Jaccard distance between placement sets as the metric where rule 0 allowed more than one | items run at `R > 1` |
| **gold fidelity** | fidelity on gold items seeded unannounced into live batches | seeded gold returned |

| **transmission after revision** | how often fresh readers holding only the revised instrument reproduce the adjudicated line, which is your own line; not reliability in the intercoder sense, and never called that | the blind sample at B4 |
| **stability** | agreement of the same reader arm with itself on the gold set under two rewordings of the brief, measured once in the pilot | the gold set |
| **position curve** | the outcome against position within batch, the drift check | items by position |
